items.topic: Synchrony Bank: two different APYs on the same official page
items.detail: Synchrony's High Yield Savings page prints 3.55% APY in the headline and again at the foot of the page, but its own savings calculator widget states 'Our HYS APY 2.85%'. This repo uses 3.55% because it is the headline and the repeated footer value. The conflict is unresolved by Synchrony's own page.
items.action: Confirm the live rate in the Synchrony app or by phone before opening.

items.topic: Chase savings APY could not be verified
items.detail: Chase's official rate page refuses to render rates without a 5-digit ZIP code ('In order to see rates table, please provide valid 5-digit zip code'). No official Chase page captured in this session printed a savings APY.
items.action: Enter the New York ZIP at chase.com to see the rate Chase will actually pay.

items.topic: Citi savings APY could not be verified
items.detail: The official Citi savings page injects the Accelerate Savings APY through a template placeholder (':BLUE_AccSavings_Rate%') that rendered no value. Citi's footnote only states that the APY is accurate as of 10/21/2026.
items.action: Check the rate inside the Citi app or with a Citi banker.

items.topic: TD Bank savings APYs could not be verified
items.detail: TD's Simple and Signature Savings rate tables render empty percentage cells until a location is selected. TD does print that 'APY is accurate as of 10/21/2026', but no number appears.
items.action: Select a New York location on TD's rate page.

items.topic: Bank of America product page rendered unfilled fee placeholders
items.detail: The Advantage Savings product page displayed '$XXXX or $0' and '$XXXX' where the monthly fee and the fee-waiver threshold belong - an unfilled template. The values shown on this site ($100 to open, $8 monthly fee, six-month new-account waiver, $500 daily-balance waiver) come from Bank of America's Personal Schedule of Fees, effective August 7, 2026, not from the product page.
items.value_not_used: the '$XXXX' placeholder on the product page
items.action: Resolved from the official fee schedule. The product page itself is still broken at capture.

items.topic: American Express National Bank FDIC certificate not retrieved
items.detail: FDIC API queries by exact name, prefix wildcard and web address all returned no institution record for American Express National Bank, so the certificate number is blank here even though Amex states 'Member FDIC' and publishes the $250,000 limit on its own pages.
items.action: Search FDIC BankFind manually; the record also appears on Amex's account agreement.

items.topic: U.S. Bank FDIC certificate not retrieved
items.detail: The FDIC certificate number for U.S. Bank, National Association was not pulled through the FDIC API in this session, so the cell is blank even though U.S. Bank advertises FDIC insurance on its savings page.
items.action: Confirm the certificate number in BankFind.

items.topic: Discover Bank is shown as inactive by the FDIC
items.detail: The FDIC API record for Discover Bank (certificate 5649, Greenwood, DE) returns ACTIVE = 0. Capital One's help centre states Discover merged into Capital One on May 18, 2025 and that from November 18, 2025 Capital One and Discover deposit accounts are jointly insured; certain Discover CDs may stay separately insured until maturity. Discover is therefore excluded from the returns tables rather than counted as a separate $250,000 stack.
items.value_used: excluded from returns tables; one combined $250,000 Capital One limit
items.action: None for a new account; do not count Capital One and Discover as two separate $250,000 banks.

items.topic: Wells Fargo rate page defaulted to a California ZIP and prints no effective date
items.detail: The captured Wells Fargo rate table was rendered for 'CA, 94105' (the page's default location), and none of the savings tables carry an effective date. A New York opening could show different numbers.
items.value_used: 3.25% APY promotional tier / 0.01% standard, as displayed
items.action: Set the ZIP to a New York ZIP before relying on the rate.

items.topic: U.S. Bank rates were displayed for ZIP 55402
items.detail: U.S. Bank's rate sheet rendered for ZIP code 55402 (Minneapolis) by default and states that 'APYs may vary by location'. The published tier structure is used here as displayed.
items.action: Edit the ZIP on the U.S. Bank rate page to a New York ZIP.

items.topic: Capital One product page rendered 'NaN APY'
items.detail: The 360 Performance Savings page displayed 'NaN APY' (a JavaScript numeric error) instead of a percentage. The 3.20% APY was taken from Capital One's own account-comparison page and application page, both of which print 3.20% APY effective 10/21/2026.
items.action: None; the alternate official page is authoritative.

items.topic: Schwab prints no effective date next to its APY (Amex resolved)
items.detail: Schwab's Investor Savings page states 0.15% APY without saying when it took effect, so its 'APY as of' cell is blank and the capture date (2026-10-22) is recorded instead. American Express was in the same position on its product page, but its information-protection page carries the disclosure 'The Annual Percentage Yield (APY) as advertised is accurate as of 10/21/2026', so Amex now shows 2026-10-21.
items.value_used: 0.15% APY (Schwab) with no as-of date; 3.20% APY as of 2026-10-21 (Amex)
items.action: Ask Schwab for its Truth-in-Savings disclosure date.

items.topic: SoFi's advertised $3M FDIC coverage is a sweep program, not a single-bank limit
items.detail: SoFi advertises FDIC insurance 'up to $3M through a network of participating banks'. A single FDIC-insured bank covers $250,000 per depositor per ownership category. Network programs depend on partner banks and program terms.
items.value_used: single-bank $250,000 used in the coverage model
items.action: Read the SoFi program terms before depositing more than $250,000 at SoFi.

items.topic: SoFi bonus tiers not fully extracted
items.detail: SoFi advertises a '$50 or $400' cash bonus with eligible direct deposit of $1,000 or more, but the exact qualifying threshold for the $400 tier is in terms that were not fully captured.
items.action: Read SoFi's bonus terms before applying.

items.topic: Marcus maximum balance limit not extracted
items.detail: Marcus states 'Maximum balance limits apply' and links to its FAQ; the numeric limit was not extracted, so no ceiling is shown in the tables.

items.topic: PNC, Fifth Third, Citizens and KeyBank: FDIC verified, savings rate not verified
items.detail: PNC, Fifth Third and Citizens FDIC records were confirmed through the FDIC API. Their savings rates / rate tables were not readable as static content in this session, so they have no row in the accounts or returns tables. KeyBank's certificate number was not confirmed, so it is excluded entirely.
items.action: Open the individual bank rate pages with a ZIP entered.

items.topic: Truist app / security claims not verified
items.detail: The Truist page captured was the savings disclosure page, which does not describe the mobile app or a security program. Those cells are blank in the Security & App table.
items.action: Review truist.com mobile banking and security pages.

items.topic: Third-party rates appear on banks' own pages and are not used
items.detail: Several official pages quote competitor or 'national average' rates sourced from Curinos / third parties (for example, Marcus' comparison widget cites Chase at 0.02% and Bank of America at 0.04%). These numbers are second-hand even though they appear on a bank site, so this repo does not use them as verification for any bank.
items.value_not_used: competitor rates quoted on bank marketing pages

items.topic: Capital One's own pages give two different start dates for joint Capital One/Discover FDIC coverage
items.detail: The 360 Performance Savings FAQ says Capital One or Discover Bank deposit accounts 'opened on or after May 18, 2025' are immediately counted together for FDIC coverage. Capital One's Discover help centre says that 'starting November 18, 2025' holders of both Capital One and Discover deposit accounts are jointly insured, with some CD exceptions. The merger closed May 18, 2025; the joint-insurance transition date is November 18, 2025.
items.value_used: November 18, 2025 (the more specific statement, from the Discover transition FAQ)
items.value_not_used: May 18, 2025 as the joint-insurance start date
items.action: Confirm current coverage in EDIE if you hold both brands.
